clue.text: These hoarders may be charged

parts.note: things that store something up and can be charged: rechargeable electric batteries, which store energy, or betting slips that roll each winning stake on

explanation.surface: Misers who pile up wealth might end up facing charges in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests an accusation, but the hoarders are storage batteries, which are charged with electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage batteries are things that pile up electrical energy and are recharged, so they are hoarders that get charged.

clue.text: Investing as a doctor, that is not heartless

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
i.e. (id est) means that is

indicators.note: the word not loses its middle letter, its heart, leaving the first and last

explanation.surface: A physician who invests money but is not without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' reads like money, but it means surrounding or enveloping. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient air surrounds or envelops everything, in the old sense of investing as clothing or enclosing.

clue.text: One of four given for the Captain of the Pinafore

definitions.text: One of four given for the Captain of the Pinafore

parts.words: One of four given for the Captain of the Pinafore
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera HMS Pinafore the crew sing 'three ... and one ... more' for their captain, four in all

explanation.surface: A tribute counted out for the commanding officer of the ship in an operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta; its chorus gives 'three cheers and one cheer more for the hardy Captain of the Pinafore'.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew's tribute is three hurrahs plus one more, so each of the four is a single shout of acclaim.

clue.text: Conciliation the middle name of the Vanity Fair man ?

definitions.text: the middle name of the Vanity Fair man ?
definitions.meaning: William ... Thackeray wrote the novel Vanity Fair

explanation.surface: A peacemaking virtue linked to the author of a famous Victorian novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a dispute is bringing peace about; and Thackeray, author of Vanity Fair, had this as his middle name.

clue.text: Sounder to go first

definitions.meaning: a weighted line dropped to measure the depth of water
to be in front, to head the way

explanation.surface: Someone more sensible ought to take the front position.
explanation.definitionFit: A sounding weight on a line measures water depth; and to head a procession is to go in front.

clue.text: Drummer leaves his mark by design

definitions.meaning: one who beats a tattoo, a drumbeat calling soldiers back to quarters
one who pricks designs into skin, marking it with a pattern on purpose

explanation.surface: A percussionist deliberately scratches his name somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating a military drum signal and inking pictures into skin both share one word, so the doer of either fits.

clue.text: Incur change of alphabet

definitions.note: the clue's noun stands for the adjective, as in the runic alphabet of the ancient Germanic peoples

indicators.note: a change of the letters of incur shuffles them into a new order

explanation.surface: Running up a cost by swapping to a different writing system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' shuffles INCUR. The runic alphabet (futhark) was used by Germanic and Norse peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes formed an old Germanic script, so this adjective describes that writing system.

clue.text: Plain Poplar

definitions.meaning: the flat lowland of the River Po in northern Italy
a tall, narrow, upright variety of poplar tree

explanation.surface: An ordinary tree, nothing fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern Italian region holds the great Po lowland, and also names the slim columnar poplar tree.

clue.text: Separate for immediate success ?

parts.note: to win is to have success
now means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: Asking to split up in exchange for instant victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. The pieces come in answer order: success (WIN) then immediate (NOW).
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers separate grain from chaff by blowing it, and figuratively one sorts good from bad the same way.

clue.text: Get off the mark quickly before catching the 8.45?

definitions.note: the morning meal is eaten before catching the 8.45 train to work

parts.note: to break is to start, as in breaking from the blocks
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A sprinter flies off the line, perhaps to catch a commuter train.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the meal by when it is eaten, before the morning train.
explanation.definitionFit: The first meal of the day is eaten before a commuter leaves for the morning train.

clue.text: Nothing in one man going back to mother-in-law

indicators.note: the word nothing goes inside the reversed letters
the letters of one man are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A man who has nothing returns to his wife's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns I MAN into NAMI, and 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, Naomi is the mother of Ruth's husband, the Bible's most famous mother-in-law.

clue.text: Delighted by parent involvement

indicators.note: an involvement of the letters of parent tangles them into a new order

explanation.surface: A father or mother is pleased to be taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involvement' is the anagram signal on PARENT; 'by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enraptured is carried away with joy, which is a strong sense of pleased.

clue.text: Rough-hewn record room ?

parts.note: a log is a record, such as a ship's log
a cabin is a room, especially on a ship

explanation.surface: A crudely built room for keeping records.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a simple hut made of rough-hewn timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer's hut is a room built of rough-hewn timber, so the whole clue paints it.

clue.text: Jack's double trouble if 18 caught

indicators.note: the word double tells us to write the sailor twice

parts.note: a jack tar, or tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's lookalike is a nuisance if he gets arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'catch a Tartar' is to take on someone who proves too much for you.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'catch a Tartar' means tackle a fierce opponent who turns the tables, so this is grief you get by catching it.

clue.text: Record to make an impression

definitions.meaning: to show or be noticed, as in a fact failing to ... with someone

explanation.surface: Writing something down to make one's mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An official roll is a list of entries; and something that sinks in or shows up on a scale is noticed.

clue.text: Boundary dispute at Sparrow's residence?

parts.note: the hedge sparrow, or dunnock, lives in hedges
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: Neighbours quarrel over the fence where a bird lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The hedge sparrow (dunnock) is a common British garden bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of shrubs marks the edge between fields, so it is a field border.

clue.text: Blouse not necessarily biscuit-coloured

parts.note: a loose red blouse named after the Italian patriot's redshirts shares its name with a currant biscuit

explanation.surface: A shirt that need not be the pale brown of a cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian hero's redshirts inspired a red blouse; the same name is a British currant biscuit, sometimes called 'squashed fly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The red shirt of an Italian patriot gave its name to a blouse, which also names a fruit biscuit.

clue.text: Plant and mark it as arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of mark it as are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Labelling a plant as part of laying out a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles MARKITAS; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This feathery shrub of coasts and dry places is a garden plant.

clue.text: Outstanding example of military discipline

parts.note: a soldier who stood out in front of a drill squad as a model for the others to copy

explanation.surface: A soldier praised as a model of drill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means literally standing out in front of the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: This trained soldier stood before the line so recruits could copy his drill, a model in the literal sense.

clue.text: Easy to find a current example in the file

indicators.note: the example goes inside the word for the file

parts.note: taken as written
AC, alternating current, is one example of a current

explanation.surface: Something simple to locate in the records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find' is a link. AC (alternating current) goes 'in' FILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile means effortless, achieved without difficulty.

clue.text: Voiced in the manner of Nicholas Nye

definitions.text: Voiced in the manner of Nicholas Nye

parts.words: Voiced in the manner of Nicholas Nye
parts.note: Nicholas Nye is the donkey in Walter de la Mare's poem, so this is the sound a donkey makes

explanation.surface: Speaking like a character in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter de la Mare's poem 'Nicholas Nye' is about an old grey donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The donkey's harsh call is a hee-haw, so speaking like the poem's donkey is making that noise.

clue.text: Red flags wielded by housemaids

parts.note: the red ensign of British merchant ships is nicknamed the red duster, and maids wave cleaning cloths

explanation.surface: Housemaids waving warning signals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Ensign, flag of the British merchant navy, is nicknamed the 'red duster'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning cloths are flapped by maids, and 'red' versions are the merchant navy flag.

clue.text: Discarded like Daniel D's hero

definitions.meaning: Daniel Defoe's Robinson Crusoe was shipwrecked alone on an island

explanation.surface: Rejected, like the shipwrecked hero of a famous novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrown aside means rejected; and Defoe's Crusoe was a shipwrecked man marooned on an island.

clue.text: All characters bet on this — the first

definitions.text: All characters bet on this — the first

parts.words: All characters bet on this — the first
parts.note: all the letters together form the ..., which is bet added to this word, the Greek first letter

explanation.surface: Everyone places a wager on the favourite to come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All characters' is the alphabet; put 'bet' on the end of this word to get it. It is also the first Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter that opens the alphabet stands for the first of anything.

clue.text: Sort of rosary for the summer?

definitions.text: Sort of rosary for the summer?

parts.words: Sort of rosary for the summer?
parts.note: a frame of beads on wires, like prayer beads, used by someone doing sums

explanation.surface: A string of prayer beads used during the warm season.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'summer' here is one who sums, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A counting frame has rows of sliding beads, like rosary beads, used for arithmetic.

clue.text: Play poet and conspirator

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar one man of this name is a poet and another a conspirator

explanation.surface: A stage drama about a poet who plots.
explanation.definitionFit: Corneille wrote a tragedy with this title; Julius Caesar has a conspirator and a poet sharing the name.

clue.text: Converted, this capital gives opportunity for abundance

definitions.text: Converted, this capital gives opportunity for abundance

parts.words: Converted, this capital gives opportunity for abundance
parts.note: the Norwegian capital's letters rearranged give the solo, a whist bid made just before abundance

explanation.surface: A city's wealth, once invested, leads to plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: In solo whist, 'solo' and 'abundance' are bids; the capital's letters rearranged spell SOLO.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital of Norway, whose letters rearranged make a card bid.

clue.text: Retire in lieu perhaps of working

definitions.meaning: go to bed or stay in bed, rest

explanation.surface: Giving up work for something else entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To rest in bed is to withdraw for the night; and staying in bed is what one might do instead of a job.

clue.text: Cheek, only entering the pub with cigarette ends

indicators.note: the word for only goes into the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
sole means only

indicators.note: the ends of cigarette are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone lights up as they walk into the pub, a cheeky move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek is rude disrespect, and insolence is just that.

clue.text: Should they be spent by the riverside?

definitions.text: Should they be spent by the riverside?

parts.words: Should they be spent by the riverside?
parts.note: public days off are named after banks, but the clue plays on river banks

explanation.surface: Wondering where public days off ought to be spent.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain public holidays are called bank holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Public days off in Britain are named after the days banks close, and a river's edge is also a bank.
